title: Dams, Straws & More
description: Turn liquid pressure into a weapon against the Baron. Water towers, straws and syringes all hide the same physics.

content.value: Cities store water in tall tanks or towers. Because pressure increases with depth (height of water), the tank being high up gives strong pressure at the taps far below. The greater the height of water above a tap, the stronger the flow.

When you suck a straw, you lower the pressure inside it. The higher pressure of the air pushing on the drink's surface then pushes the liquid UP the straw into your mouth. It's really pressure difference doing the work.

Sucking a straw:
😮  you reduce pressure inside the straw
🌬️  outside air pressure pushes down on the drink
⬆️  the drink is pushed up the straw!

A syringe or a dropper works the same way. Squeeze the bulb to push air out, then release — the pressure inside drops and liquid rushes in to fill the space. Push the plunger and higher pressure forces the liquid back out.
Many 'sucking' actions are really PUSHING actions — the surrounding air or liquid at higher pressure pushes into the low-pressure space you created.
Key Takeaway: Liquid pressure powers water supplies (height gives pressure), while pressure differences let us drink through straws and draw liquid into syringes and droppers.

quiz.question: Water towers are built TALL because…
options: greater height of water gives more pressure at the taps
quiz.explain: Pressure increases with the height (depth) of water, so a tall tower delivers strong pressure to taps below.

quiz.question: When you drink through a straw, the liquid rises because…
options: you pull it up with a special force
outside air pressure pushes it up into the low-pressure straw
quiz.explain: Sucking lowers the pressure inside the straw; higher outside air pressure then pushes the drink up.

quiz.question: A dropper fills with liquid when you release the squeezed bulb because…
options: pressure inside drops and liquid is pushed in to fill the space
quiz.explain: Releasing the bulb lowers the inside pressure, so higher outside pressure pushes liquid into the dropper.
